name: Symbolic spelling correction before the small formalizer
registered_by: eval agent (owner request of 2026-09-29: CPU-only evaluation experiment; no training, no GPU)
frozen_before_results: Written after the corrector was developed and tuned on the formalizer-v1 development split only, and before the corrector or any spellfixed prediction touched any sealed suite (formalizer-v1 test, formalizer-ood-v1, formalizer-wild-v1). Any later change to the corrector, the conditions, the metrics or the decision rule is a recorded deviation.
kind: evaluation-only (inference on CPU with an existing checkpoint; no optimizer step, no training data change)
question: Does a deterministic, dictionary-based spelling correction of the user's message, applied by the host before the small formalizer, improve formalization of noisy messages without hurting clean ones?

hypotheses.H1: On formalizer-v1 sealed-test rows with labelled typing noise (noise_level light, medium or heavy), SmolLM2-135M (fv1-size-a4, Q8_0) reaches higher tolerant execution equivalence on the spellfixed message than on the raw message.
hypotheses.H2: On clean formalizer-v1 test rows (noise_level null) the spellfixed condition is non-inferior: the paired delta of tolerant execution equivalence has a 95% interval lower bound >= -0.5 points.
hypotheses.H3: The corrector alone has precision >= 0.90 on verifiable changes and changes at most 1% of clean messages.

changed_factor: The message given to the model: raw (as written) versus the output of lib/spellfix.mjs spellfix-v1. Model, weights, quantization, runtime, decoding and scoring are identical.
comparator: The existing raw-message Q8_0 predictions of formalizer-size-v1 arm smollm2-135m (reused, not regenerated).

corrector.resources: Hunspell en_US (SCOWL 2020.12.07, npm dictionary-en 4.0.0, MIT AND BSD) and ro (Rospell 3.3.10, npm dictionary-ro 3.0.0, GPL-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1 OR MPL-1.1) from wooorm/dictionaries@8cfea406b505e4d7df52d5a19bce525df98c54ab; unigram frequencies hermitdave/FrequencyWords@525f9b560de45753a5ea01069454e72e9aa541c6 content/2018/{en,ro}/*_full.txt (OpenSubtitles 2018; code MIT, content CC BY-SA 4.0). Recorded in dependencies.md; kept in the git-ignored vendor/spellfix/.
corrector.policy: Changes only words in neither dictionary nor the 20,000 most frequent words of either list; keyboard-aware single edits (QWERTY, Romanian standard layout, diacritic substitutions), split of two merged words, merge of a word split by a space, diacritic restoration; a known word is restored to a diacritic variant only in a Romanian message typed without any diacritic and when the variant is >= 5x more frequent. Never touched: capitalized tokens (except a sentence-initial word absent from the frequency lists and corrected into one of the 500 most frequent words), all-caps, numbers, dates, e-mails, URLs, tokens with digits, quoted text, hyphenated/apostrophized tokens, words shorter than 4 letters (except diacritic restoration), letters repeated three times, contractions typed without an apostrophe, and messages whose lower-case words are mostly unknown and one edit away from nothing known (gibberish). Never produces a negation or quantifier cue word. Every change is logged.
corrector.development: Tuned on datasets/formalizer-v1/dev.jsonl only (sha256 86c85e9aa12a9bade23e4c8453b694f57838ab7022ecc67949f524a6ffdd88f2): grid costWeight {2,3,4} x margin {0.5,0.7,1.0}; the most precise setting was chosen. Development report eval/reports/current/spellfix/dev-quality.json: verifiable precision 0.944, non-word recall 0.601, 2 of 3,577 clean messages changed.

model.runtime: llama.cpp ~/llama-cpp-venv/llama.cpp commit 99d4026b116605ed8e1f3ab179b3c63bc4637195, llama-server -ngl 0 --jinja -np 4 -c 32768, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty (no GPU), 8 threads (the raw condition used 16; greedy output does not depend on the thread count, checked by the rerun control)
model.harness: tools/research/predict-endpoint.mjs (sha256 d9fba00afa31dc93517f833e9916a08127ab1600a76219830cab0e45703b2ad2), message as the only user turn, temperature 0, top_k 1, max_tokens 6144, parallel 4
model.conditional_arm: gemma (formalizer-size-v1 arm 2) under the same protocol, raw and spellfixed, only if its Q8_0 GGUF exists within this session; otherwise deferred and reported as not run

procedure: 1. Corrector quality on each suite (tools/research/spellfix-eval.mjs quality): every change logged.

2. Build the spellfixed condition: only rows whose message the corrector changes are predicted again (spellfix-eval.mjs apply, then predict-endpoint.mjs on those rows); an unchanged row has an identical input and keeps its raw prediction (spellfix-eval.mjs merge). All rows are used; no sampling.

3. Rerun control: 300 unchanged short formalizer-v1 rows (predict-endpoint.mjs --sample 300 --seed 42 on the unchanged set) are predicted again under the new server settings; the share of byte-identical outputs is reported as the run-to-run noise floor.
4. Score both conditions with the same scorer (tools/metrics/run.mjs for formalizer-v1 and OOD; tools/eval/wild-suite.mjs --score for wild) and compare paired (spellfix-eval.mjs compare).

metrics.primary: Tolerant execution equivalence (DS016, execution_equivalent_tolerant) on formalizer-v1 test noisy rows, paired delta spellfixed minus raw.
secondary: the same delta on clean rows (H2), per noise level (none, light, medium, heavy), per language slice (en, ro, mixed), and per noise level x language
canonical AST match and parse rate deltas
formalizer-wild-v1 accepted-gold match, decision match and proposition F1 (per-row, paired)
rows changed by the corrector versus unchanged
corrector: precision on verifiable changes (exact undo of a recorded word-level noise operation; changes with only a character-level diacritic record are reported separately as unverifiable)
recall of recorded word-level operations (all, non-word, real-word)
damage: share of clean messages changed and changes per 1,000 tokens
synthetic diacritic restoration on clean Romanian rows (diacritics stripped from lower-case words)
latency per message (ms, p50/p95/p99) on this CPU, one thread, after loading
metrics.uncertainty: 95% paired cluster bootstrap (clusters = semantic_case_id, 10,000 resamples, seed 7) and exact McNemar test on rows; the wild suite clusters by row.

decision_rule: Recommend adoption as a host pre-step only if all hold: (a) the primary delta is positive and its 95% interval excludes 0; (b) H2 holds (clean-row lower bound >= -0.5 points); (c) the formalizer-ood-v1 noisy-row delta and the wild accepted-match delta are not significantly negative (interval upper bound >= 0); (d) H3 holds. If (a) fails but (b)-(d) hold, the conclusion is 'no measurable benefit' and the recommendation is not to adopt. Any significantly negative primary or clean delta means 'harmful, do not adopt'.
limitations_declared: The model was fine-tuned on noisy messages whose gold role values keep typos (DS022 target policy), so correction can move a role value away from the gold string; tolerant execution equivalence links strings to knowledge and is the primary endpoint for that reason, while canonical match is reported as secondary.
Real-word errors (dictation homophones, autocorrect, SMS forms) are out of scope for a dictionary corrector by construction.
The formalizer-v1 noise is synthetic; formalizer-wild-v1 has real user text but no noise labels and no execution worlds.
Single model and seed; experiment-grade, no human review.

budget.hardware: CPU only (GB10 host, 20 cores shared with another CPU evaluation), GPU forbidden (a training run owns it)
budget.abort: stop if the host shows memory pressure or the GPU would be touched
